The task: Identify the product as either of four given formulas based on NMR (triplet, quartet, singlet) and mass peaks at m/z=30 and 58. The response gave final answer CH3CH2NHCOOCH3 (ethyl carbamate). Need to see if that matches the data.

Let's analyze each candidate:

1) CH3OCH2CONHCH3: structure: methoxyacetamide? Actually CH3-O-CH2-CO-NH-CH3. NMR: CH3-O (singlet? maybe ~3.3), CH2 next to O (maybe quartet? Actually CH2 attached to O and carbonyl: could be a singlet? Not sure). NHCH3 maybe broad. Not likely to give triplet, quartet, singlet.

2) CH3NHCOOCH2CH3: ethyl carbamate (NH-CO-O-CH2-CH3). NMR: NH (broad, exchangeable not observed), CH3 of NH (singlet?), CH2 of ethyl (quartet? Actually CH2 next to O gives quartet? Wait ethyl group O-CH2-CH3: CH2 adjacent to O and CH3 gives quartet? Actually CH2 next to O and CH3: CH2 sees CH3 (3H) => quartet; CH3 sees CH2 (2H) => triplet. So we would expect quartet (CH2) and triplet (CH3). Plus singlet for N-CH3. That matches triplet, quartet, singlet. Good. Exchangeable NH not observed. So fits.

Mass spec: m/z=30 could be CH2NH2+? Actually fragment maybe NH2CH2+? m/z=30 could be CH2NH2+ (mass 30). m/z=58 could be CH3CH2OCO
